about.headline: No one could put a logo on my business card
about.lead: I became a planner because a tax law changed my career before it started.
story: I studied construction and finance. I was going to build commercial real estate. Then, right as I graduated, a new tax law made construction and development "a ghost town." Plans that looked solid one year were gone the next.
So I moved into a field that was brand new at the time: financial planning. I've spent my career since then helping people plan around the things that change: tax laws, markets, and life.

Early on I made one decision that shaped everything: no one could put a logo on my business card. I wanted to work for my clients, not for a company's products. Over the years I've also been a landlord and bought and sold businesses, so I know "tenants and toilets" firsthand, and I treat your rentals and your business as part of your plan, not competition for it.

Today my office is three companies working together: Balanced Financial for insurance and legacy planning, Fort Collins Tax Advisory Group for tax preparation and advice, and Balanced Wealth Partners for investments. Your tax return, your documents and your investments sit at one table.
about.calling: What I love most is the moment a couple realizes the worry is gone, because they finally have a path to run on.

planning.title: Retirement Income Planning
planning.card_text: Turn your savings into income that lasts for both of you.
planning.seo_title: Retirement Income Planning in Fort Collins, CO
planning.h1: Retirement Income Planning in Fort Collins
planning.lead: You don't need a bigger number. You need a paycheck plan.
belief: Most people approach retirement asking, "Have we saved enough?" It's a fair question, and it's the wrong one.
The question that matters is, "Where does our paycheck come from every month, for both of us, for as long as we live?"
familiar: You don't know how much you can take out each year
You haven't decided when each of you will claim Social Security
You've never seen your retirement income on one page

ideas.title: Your paycheck, not your pile
ideas.text: Start with what you'll spend and the income you can count on. The gap is what your savings must cover.

ideas.title: The first years matter most
ideas.text: A market drop right after you retire hurts more than the same drop ten years later, because you're withdrawing at the same time.

ideas.title: Plan for two people
ideas.text: Social Security choices and survivor income decide what the surviving spouse lives on.

planning.how: Step 1 of the PATH Plan, Paycheck, puts your whole retirement income on one page: your Retirement Paycheck Map.

faq.q: When should we take Social Security?
faq.a: It depends on your health, your spouse and your other income. Greg teaches Social Security strategy, and we'll run your options in your PATH Review.

planning.title: Investments, Risk & Long-Term Care
planning.card_text: Give your money jobs, and plan for long-term care.
planning.seo_title: Retirement Risk & Long-Term Care Planning | Fort Collins
planning.h1: Investment Risk and Long-Term Care Planning
planning.lead: The stock market helps you build savings. In retirement it can hurt you, if the wrong money is in the wrong place.
belief: Most retirement portfolios are still built the way they were at 45: for growth.
Once you're taking income, the money you'll live on in the next few years needs a different job than the money you won't touch for fifteen.
familiar: All your money is invested the same way
You don't know your risk score
You have no plan for long-term care

ideas.title: Money by purpose
ideas.text: Income money, growth money and reserve money, each positioned for its job.

ideas.title: Know your number
ideas.text: Your risk score shows how much a market drop could move your plan.

ideas.title: Long-term care is a plan, not a policy
ideas.text: Home care, assisted living and nursing care can be planned for in several ways, including from your own assets.

planning.how: Step 2 of the PATH Plan, Assets, gives you a Risk & Reserve Report.

planning.title: Retirement Tax Planning
planning.card_text: Your 401(k) isn't all yours. Plan when the IRS collects.
planning.seo_title: Retirement Tax Planning in Fort Collins, CO
planning.h1: Retirement Tax Planning in Fort Collins
planning.lead: Part of your 401(k) belongs to the IRS. The rules decide when they collect, unless you plan first.
belief: Most people assume taxes go down in retirement. For good savers, they often don't.
Required withdrawals, Social Security taxation and Medicare surcharges can stack up in the same years. Planning the years before that is where the opportunity is.
familiar: Most of your savings is pre-tax
You've heard about Roth conversions but no one has run your numbers
Your tax preparer and your advisor never talk
You have restricted stock and you're not sure when to sell

ideas.title: Required withdrawals start later now, and get bigger
ideas.text: Required minimum distributions now start at 73, or 75 for anyone born in 1960 or later, so balances can keep growing pre-tax until then.

ideas.title: Medicare looks back two years
ideas.text: Medicare Part B and D surcharges are based on your income from two years earlier, so a big conversion or sale this year can raise your premiums later.

ideas.title: Your return is the map
ideas.text: Our tax team starts with your actual return and runs "what if" scenarios: conversions, withdrawals, RSU sales, rental or business sales.

planning.how: Step 3 of the PATH Plan, Taxes, gives you a CPA What-If Tax Timeline built from your own return.
planning.note: Tax services are provided by Fort Collins Tax Advisory Group, LLC. Tax rules change; the figures here are current as of 2026 and are educational, not tax advice for your situation.

faq.q: Should I do a Roth conversion?
faq.a: Sometimes yes, sometimes no. It depends on your bracket now and later, your Medicare premiums and your heirs. That's what the CPA What-If review is for.

planning.title: Estate Planning
planning.card_text: Protect your spouse and kids on paper, and keep your family out of court.
planning.seo_title: Estate Planning Help in Fort Collins, CO
planning.h1: Estate Planning Coordination in Fort Collins
planning.lead: A plan isn't about how much you have. It's about who decides when you can't, and whether your family ends up in court.
belief: Many families think estate planning is about estate tax. In Colorado, for most families, it isn't: Colorado has no estate or inheritance tax, and the federal exemption is very high.
It's about incapacity, court time, and getting money to the right people without a fight. That's the part most people miss.
familiar: Your will was signed years ago, or you don't have one
You're not sure who your beneficiaries are
You have a family member who needs special care or protection
You own rentals or property in another state

ideas.title: A will doesn't keep you out of probate court
ideas.text: Some assets pass by beneficiary form or title. Others, like a home in your name alone, may go through the court [ATTORNEY REVIEW].

ideas.title: Incapacity is the part most people miss
ideas.text: Durable powers of attorney and medical directives let the right people act for you without a court.

ideas.title: Beneficiary forms usually win
ideas.text: An old beneficiary form can override what your will says. Check them every time life changes.

faq.q: Should I sell my rentals before I retire?
faq.a: It depends on the tax, the income they produce and how much work they are. We'll run the numbers with you.
